title: Renewal Sprint Tactics and Seat Growth Hypotheses
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sprint playbook for execution-level QBR prep, lightweight renewal tracking, and 3-week experiment cycles to generate lift for Dedicated upgrades, Private deployments, and premium SLA add-ons. Intended for CS reps + solutions engineers running medium-to-large renewal motions (ARR $75k+).

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineering (SE) and Sales Engineers
- Account Executives (for co-sell handoffs)
- Customer Reliability / Security reviewers for Private offers

TL;DR (one-liner):
Run short hypothesis-led sprints that combine an operational renewal tracker, two QBR templates (executive + technical), and low-effort conversion catalysts (trial dedicated slot, cost model, and security readiness checklist) to close upgrades within 6–12 weeks.

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Run a 3-week sprint per account with the renewal scorecard filled on day 1.
2) Use the executive QBR template for business stakeholders; technical QBR for SRE/security.
3) Hypothesis experiments (A/B): pricing anchoring vs. immediate dedicated trial; technical POC vs. security-only review.
4) Log outcomes and next experiments in the renewal tracker.

Renewal / Upsell Scorecard (fill on Day 1):
- ARR band: (string) e.g., $150k
- Primary use-case: short description
- Current deployment mode: Hosted | Dedicated (size) | Private
- Renewal horizon: YYYY-MM-DD
- Expansion target: Dedicated upgrade / Private deployment / SLA add-on
- Exec sponsor health: High | Medium | Low (notes)
content_more:
- Churn risk signals: list (support tickets, latency spikes, usage drop)
- Top 3 blocker hypotheses: 1) Cost concerns, 2) Security/compliance, 3) Migration effort

Executive QBR template (30–45 min):
- Objective: surface business impact and cost-benefit of upgrade.
- Attendees: VP Product / Head of AI, CSM, SE, Finance contact (if present)
- Agenda:
  1) Opening (3 min): recap usage and business KPI tied to LLM features
  2) Impact summary (7 min): tokens/month, cost/month, latency/SLO deviations, key wins
  3) Expansion proposal (10 min): dedicated capacity uplift or Private deployment benefits (isolation, SLAs, throughput), topline estimated delta in latency/cost/service availability
  4) Commercial ask (7 min): proposed term, pricing band, pilot commitment, and ROI math (show incremental token cost and unit economics)
  5) Next steps (5 min): decision owner, technical POC window, legal/security contacts

Technical QBR / Security Review (60 min):
- Objective: align on architecture, data flows, security controls, and deployment timeline.
- Attendees: CS technical lead, customer SRE/security, customer infra lead, Redwood SE, infra ops
- Agenda highlights:
  - Current infra and traffic patterns (throughput, peak concurrency)
  - Dedicated capacity sizing recommendation (GPU types, concurrency targets, expected p99 latency)
  - Network topology and private link/VPC details (egress rules, CIDR, NAT, bastion options)
  - Data residency and encryption controls (KMS/HSM recommendations)
  - Migration window estimate and rollback plan
  - SLA uplift matrix (SLA tier vs. credit/penalty and response times)

Renewal Tracker (one-line per account; rep-owned):
- Columns (pseudo-table line): account | rep | ARR | renewal_date | target_offer | score | last_touch | next_action | blockers | notes | hypothesis_id
- Example line: Acme Bio | Diego A. | $220,000 | 2025-06-30 | Dedicated-4x | 78 | 2025-02-25 | Exec QBR 2025-03-03 | security review | trial-dedicated-14d

Sprint Plan (3-week cadence):
- Week 0 (prep): fill scorecard, book exec + technical QBR windows, pre-send one-pager and cost delta
- Week 1 (engage): run exec QBR, capture commercial stance, spin up trial dedicated slot if agreed
- Week 2 (prove): run technical QBR, complete security checklist, collect logs/metrics from trial, calculate measured p50/p95/p99 changes
- Week 3 (close/extend): present measured ROI, finalize BA/contract addendum or schedule next experiment

Low-friction conversion levers (playbook items):
- 14-day dedicated trial with pre-sized GPU pool and pre-approved terms
- Prebuilt cost delta model (spreadsheet snippet to paste in QBR)
- Security readiness checklist with clear gating items (KMS key owner, SOC2 artifacts, network allowlist)
- Migration timebox offer: 2-week migration with embedded SE hours (discounted)

Hypothesis library (A/B test friendly):
- H1: If we offer a 14-day dedicated trial with observed p95 improvement, conversion rate increases by 30% vs price discount.
- H2: If we pre-supply a security artifact pack (attestation + network design) conversion time shortens by 40%.
- H3: If we present a 12-month committed pricing vs month-to-month, ARR uplift is 12% but time-to-sign increases 2 weeks.

Risk matrix (short):
- Cost pushback: counter with measured per-token delta and estimated cost/latency ROI for 6–12 months
- Security/legal stop: surface required docs and schedule a 1:1 with security reviewer within 3 business days
- Data residency: escalate to Private deployment track and involve product infra PM for feasibility

Sample outreach templates (short):
- Exec invite subject: "QBR: [Customer] — Performance and capacity proposal (15–30 min)"
- Exec invite body: quick bullets: usage, headline improvement we can deliver, ask (decision-maker + finance), attach 1-page cost delta
- Technical invite subject: "SRE sync: Private/Dedicated migration design review"
- Technical invite body: attach network checklist, desired logs for day 0, target p99 SLA

Commercial and pricing guidance (rep quick-check):
- Pricing bands: small uplift (10–18% on hosted token rate) for Dedicated entry tier; Private/enterprise deployment priced as platform fee + commit (example: $30k/mo platform + committed GPU hrs). Always tie to usage economics in the deck.
- Negotiation play: hold on platform fee discount but offer 3 months free SE hours for migration.

Security readiness checklist (for Private / dedicated offers):
- SOC2 artifacts available: yes/no (link)
- KMS/HSM integration required: yes/no
- Network allowlist process documented: yes/no (owner contact)
- Data export/export controls: notes
- Audit log retention and access plan

Measurement and KPIs (what success looks like):
- Primary: conversion rate from sprint to closed uplift (goal 25% per sprint cohort)
- Secondary: time-to-sign (goal < 8 weeks), average uplift ARR per converted account (goal +$125k), measured p95 improvement

Playbook operational notes (CS ops):
- Use ticket prefix: CS-RENEW-sprint-YYYYMM for all artifacts
- Store trial results folder in Drive under shared_drives/customer-success/experiments/YYYYMM
- Update CRM milestone: QBR-scheduled, QBR-run, Technical-proved, Contract-sent, Closed-won/lose + reason

Open questions / TODOs (for this draft):
- Formal pilot T&Cs for 14-day dedicated trial (legal needs draft)
- Sample cost delta spreadsheet (need engineering input on realistic p95 gains by GPU class)
- SLA uplift legal language (template)

Next steps (who does what):
- Maya Chen: finalize security checklist with Priya (due 2025-03-05)
- Diego Alvarez: prototype 14-day trial orchestration runbook (due 2025-03-07)
- Ethan Brooks: build cost-delta spreadsheet draft and sample p95 numbers (due 2025-03-10)

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep templates short — execs hate long decks. Focus on business KPIs + one clear ask.
- For mid-market accounts, favor price anchoring + 3-month SE credit over full Private migration pitch.
- Track failed experiments with a short root-cause note (copy to experiments folder).

Appendix: quick links and artifacts to attach in invites
